page.layout: One page of text, one column. Above the column: a decorative woodcut ornament, then a centred two-line title in capitals and small capitals. Below: two stanzas of italic verse, the first opening with a large woodcut initial. A faint, mirrored running head at the top is show-through and is left out.

main_text.head: IDEM SIMEONIS CANTICVM PARAPHRASI POETICA I. I. B. expressum.

p.i:
CVM te puellum Christe senilibus Excepit vlnis debilior Simon, Clarus propinqua morte vates Tale pio dedit ore carmen.
Nunc lata venit, summe Parens, dies: Nunc me solutum corpore liberans Promissa praestas, seruulumq; ue [?] Pace tuum potiore donas.
Sperata priscis nam tua patribus Nunc missa cælo conspicitur salus [?] Gaudente: praesentémque nostris Illam oculis licet intueri.
Illam statuto tempore Gentibus Cunctis fruendam nunc, Pater, obiicis: Quacunque Sol feruens iacentes Purpureo fouet igne terras:
Quae caeca falsis religionibus [?] Nox ante plebes implicuit vagas, Iam pulsa vanescet: per orbem Luce tua radiante totum.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "seruulumq; ue" (printed "ferunulúmq ue"); "cælo" (printed with a ligature, possibly "cœlo" or "caelo"); "fouet" (printed with a worn letter); "falsis" in the line "Quae caeca ... religionibus" (printed "f.Elis", hard to read). The woodcut initial is a C, joined to "CVM". The faint line at the top of the page is show-through from the reverse and is not transcribed.
